The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run** example that creates a new Compute Engine VM on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with:

| Requirement | How it’s satisfied |
|-------------|--------------------|
| **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX A6000 | `--accelerator type=nvidia-a6000,count=1` |
| **OS** – Ubuntu 20.04 LTS | `--image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud` |
| **Machine type** – balanced CPU & memory (you can change it later) | `--machine-type=e2-standard-8` |
| **Boot disk size** – 50 GB (adjustable) | `--boot-disk-size=50GB` |
| **Zone** – pick one that supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-b`) | `--zone=us-central1-b` |

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI Command

```bash
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
    --project=my-gcp-project-id \
    --zone=us-central1-b \
    --machine-type=e2-standard-8 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=50GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --boot-disk-device-name=my-rtx-a6000-disk \
    --accelerator type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
    --tags=http-server,https-server \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --service-account=my-service-account@my-gcp-project-id.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--project` | Your GCP project ID |
| `--zone` | Zone that supports GPUs (`us-central1-b`, `us-east1-c`, etc.) |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/memory profile (e.g., `e2-standard-8` gives 8 vCPU + 32 GB RAM) |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk |
| `--boot-disk-type` | Balanced persistent disk (`pd-balanced`) |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Keep the instance running during maintenance events |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts if the instance crashes |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional script that runs at first boot (e.g., install drivers) |
| `--tags` | Network tags for firewall rules |
| `--scopes` | Permissions for the instance |
| `--service-account` | Service account to run under (optional but recommended) |

> **Tip:**  
> *If you don’t have a service account yet, create one via IAM → Service Accounts → Create Service Account.*  
> *Make sure the account has the “Compute Admin” role or at least the permissions needed to attach GPUs.*

---

## 2️⃣  REST API Call (JSON)

If you prefer to use the REST API directly (or via Terraform, Pulumi, etc.), here’s the exact JSON payload you would POST to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json
```

### Request Body

```json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000",
  "machineType": "projects/my-gcp-project-id/zones/us-central1-b/machineTypes/e2-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project-id/zones/us-central1-b/diskTypes/pd-balanced",
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      },
      "deviceName": "my-rtx-a6000-disk",
      "mode": "READ_WRITE",
      "type": "PERSISTENT"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "my-service-account@my-gcp-project-id.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project-id/zones/us-central1-b/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

> **Replace placeholders** (`{PROJECT_ID}`, `{ZONE}`, `{ACCESS_TOKEN}`) with your actual values.

---

## 3️⃣  Quick Checklist Before Running

1. **Enable APIs**  
   * Compute Engine API  
   * Cloud Resource Manager API  
   * Cloud Billing API (if you’re using billing quotas)

2. **Check GPU Quotas**  
   * Go to **IAM & Admin → Quotas** → filter for “NVIDIA A6000” → ensure you have enough quota in the selected zone.

3. **Billing Enabled**  
   * Make sure your project has an active billing account attached.

4. **Firewall Rules**  
   * The tags `http-server` and `https-server` automatically allow inbound traffic on ports 80/443 if you’ve enabled the default firewall rules.  
   * If you need other ports (e.g., 22 for SSH), add them manually.

5. **Service Account Permissions**  
   * At minimum, grant the service account the **Compute Instance Admin (v1)** role.

---

## 4️⃣  After Creation

Once the instance is up:

* **SSH into it**  
  ```bash
  gcloud compute ssh my-rtx-a6000 --zone us-central1-b
  ```

* **Verify GPU**  
  ```bash
  nvidia-smi
  ```

* **Install CUDA Toolkit** (if required)  
  ```bash
  sudo apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-12-1
  ```

* **Optional: Install Docker**  
  ```bash
  sudo apt-get install -y docker.io
  sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
  ```

---

### 🎉 Done!  

You now have a fully functional GCP VM with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. Happy computing!
